Round 2 · Implementation · Hard

Ticket #12 — Digital Wallet Ledger

Difficulty: Hard

Context

You maintain transfers between two digital wallets. Amounts are in cents. The ledger is the saved history of movements: a debit is a negative entry in the source wallet, and the matching credit is a positive entry in the destination. A wallet balance is its opening funds plus all its entries.

Practice report

Open w-1 with 5000 cents and w-2 with 1000 cents. Call transfer("tx-2", "w-1", "w-2", 300) twice, representing a client retry.

Observation Current starter Expected
Source balance 4400 4700
Destination balance 1600 1300
Entries for tx-2 4 2

The entries still sum to zero in the starter; the problem is the extra movement for one transaction ID.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Each new posted transfer writes exactly one debit and one matching credit; those two amounts sum to zero and move the requested amount between wallets.
  • A transfer needs a positive amount, distinct existing wallets, and sufficient source funds. A rejected transfer leaves both balances and all entries unchanged.
  • An exact transaction-ID replay returns posted without moving funds or appending entries again.
  • Reusing a transaction ID for a different source, destination, or amount returns conflict and preserves its original entries and wallet balances.
  • No accepted new transfer overdraws the source wallet. Ledger history and derived balances must agree after each operation.

Out of Scope

Use the local ledger and supplied numeric amounts. Bank settlement, fees, currency conversion, transaction authentication, and distributed storage are outside this ticket.

Investigation

Reproduce the duplicate request and inspect transaction entries alongside both balances. Add regression tests for exact replay, conflicting reuse, insufficient funds, and the same-wallet case. Explain why balanced entries alone do not prove that a transfer happened only once.
